name: Breuil-Cervinia (Cervino Ski Paradise)

source.note: Piste reference data — confirm at source. Approximate Breuil-Cervinia village

Search summary: village 2,050 m; skiing to 3,480 m at Plateau Rosa. The linked international area spans 1,524–3,883 m (lowest point likely Valtournenche; top Klein Matterhorn, per the Zermatt search). Vertical derived as the difference. Search summary did not tie this to one result; cited URL is the most likely source.

Figures describe the whole linked Matterhorn ski paradise (Zermatt + Breuil-Cervinia + Valtournenche). Lift types per the skiresort.info listing (search summary): 1 cog railway, 2 funiculars, 8 aerial tramways, 11 gondolas, 1 combined gondola/chair installation, 22 chairlifts, 6 T-bars = 51 lifts ('other' = cog railway + 2 funiculars + combined installation; 3 people movers and 7 moving carpets are also listed but not counted in the 51). Uphill capacity 96,074 persons/hour (same listing). Pistes: up to 360 km, of which 74 km blue, 220 km red and 64 km black (search summary); percentages derived from those km (blue = beginner, red = intermediate, black = advanced). Other results: Zermatt alone 52 lifts; Matterhorn ski paradise 54 lifts and 'over 90,000' persons/hour. Italian-side-only figures were not found. A Cervinia search summary said 72 lifts and 'over 360 km'.
Piste reference data — confirm at source. Ski schools and rental shops operate in Breuil-Cervinia; other features not on file

character: High-altitude Italian resort below the Matterhorn (Monte Cervino) in the Aosta Valley, linked over the Plateau Rosa/Theodul glacier to Zermatt and down to Valtournenche. Long, mostly intermediate runs start as high as 3,480 m, and the Matterhorn Alpine Crossing gondola connects with Zermatt.
learning: Reference note: wide, gentle upper slopes and ski schools in the village. Confirm beginner areas and lesson products.
